proposal.title: Ulynmib: a routing daemon for community mesh networks
proposal.summary: Ulynmib builds a routing daemon for community mesh networks for community network groups.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Mesh networks lose routes when nodes move or fail. Community network groups depend on mesh networking every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a routing daemon for community mesh networks called Ulynmib. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Mesh networking is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/ulynmib/ulynmib, which 175 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on mesh networking for 5 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the MPL-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/ulynmib/ulynmib. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 33650.00 EUR for 50 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Mesh networks lose routes when nodes move or fail. Community network groups depend on mesh networking every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a routing daemon for community mesh networks called Ulynmib. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Mesh networking is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/ulynmib/ulynmib, which 175 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on mesh networking for 5 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the MPL-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/ulynmib/ulynmib. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

Budget justification
